name: Northeast Arête
descent_text: The arete ends on the summit, and the way off is the standard Southwest Route. A short rappel of roughly 35 to 40 ft down the summit block, from slings in the notch between the summit pillars, returns you to the ridge; a 30 m rope is plenty. Below that, loose scree and talus on the southwest side leads back toward Snowy Lakes, and plunge-stepping makes it quick. From camp, retrace the Pacific Crest Trail over Granite Pass and Cutthroat Pass to Rainy Pass.
approach: Same general Snowy Lakes basecamp approach as the standard route (PCT from Rainy Pass), continuing to the base of the northeast side of the peak; expect to find your own way from there.
overview: A five-pitch, III 5.8 alpine rock route up Golden Horn's northeast arête, first climbed by Gordy Skoog and Jim Walseth in 1979.
beta: A moderate, multi-pitch line following the arête on the mountain's northeast side. The rock looks classic but climbs 'shaky,' with numerous fragile flakes of dubious stability and protection that is sometimes insecure.
fa: Gordy Skoog and Jim Walseth — August 8, 1979
